subproblem.title: Carrier minus support is H^n-null (Simon 4.10(1); positivity of theta)
subproblem.statement: Let U be any subset of R^(n+l) and V = v(M, theta) a rectifiable n-varifold in U (contract structure: M ⊆ U, M H^n-null-measurable, theta > 0 on M, theta a.e.-measurable for H^n restricted to M). Its weight is mu = V.weight = (H^n restricted to M) with density ofReal(theta), and spt V = U ∩ spt mu. Then H^n(M \ spt V) = 0, where H^n = muHE[n]. No density hypothesis and no openness of U is assumed.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} {U : Set (Amb n ℓ)} (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U), (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (V.carrier \ V.support) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1(b) and 2 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 4, Remark 4.10(1): spt V versus the carrier M).

Notation: H^n = muHE[n] on X = R^(n+l); M = V.carrier ⊆ U; theta = V.mult; mu = V.weight = (H^n restricted to M) with density x -> ofReal(theta(x)) (Mathlib withDensity); spt mu = V.weight.support, the points all of whose neighbourhoods have positive mu-measure; spt V = U ∩ spt mu. No density hypothesis, no openness of U and no restriction on n is used.

1. Reduction. Let O := X \ spt mu. If x ∈ M \ spt V, then x ∉ spt mu. Otherwise x ∈ U (because M ⊆ U, field carrier_subset) and x ∈ spt mu, so x ∈ U ∩ spt mu = spt V, a contradiction. Hence M \ spt V ⊆ O ∩ M, and by monotonicity it suffices to prove H^n(O ∩ M) = 0.
2. O is open, because spt mu is closed (Measure.isClosed_support). In particular O is a Borel (measurable) set.
3. mu(O) = 0. Every point of O has an open neighbourhood of mu-measure 0, by definition of the support. X is second countable, hence hereditarily Lindelof, so countably many of these neighbourhoods cover O. Countable subadditivity gives mu(O) = 0 (Measure.measure_compl_support).
4. Since O is measurable, mu(O) = ∫_O ofReal(theta) d(H^n restricted to M) (withDensity_apply). Also (H^n restricted to M) restricted to O equals H^n restricted to O ∩ M (Measure.restrict_restrict, O measurable). Hence ∫ ofReal(theta) d(H^n restricted to O ∩ M) = 0.
5. The function x -> ofReal(theta(x)) is a.e.-measurable for H^n restricted to O ∩ M. Indeed, theta is a.e.-measurable for H^n restricted to M (field aemeasurable_mult); H^n restricted to O ∩ M ≤ H^n restricted to M since O ∩ M ⊆ M (Measure.restrict_mono); and ofReal preserves a.e.-measurability. A nonnegative a.e.-measurable function with zero integral vanishes almost everywhere (lintegral_eq_zero_iff'). So ofReal(theta(x)) = 0 for almost every x with respect to H^n restricted to O ∩ M.
6. O ∩ M is H^n-null-measurable, since O is open and M is H^n-null-measurable (field nullMeasurableSet_carrier). Therefore (ae_restrict_iff'₀), for H^n-a.e. x: if x ∈ O ∩ M then ofReal(theta(x)) = 0, i.e. theta(x) ≤ 0.
7. But theta(x) > 0 for every x ∈ M (field mult_pos). Hence for H^n-a.e. x we have x ∉ O ∩ M. That is, the complement of O ∩ M is H^n-conull, so H^n(O ∩ M) = 0 (mem_ae_iff).
8. By step 1 and monotonicity, H^n(M \ spt V) ≤ H^n(O ∩ M) = 0.
proof_key_steps: M \ spt V ⊆ O ∩ M with O = complement of spt mu, because M ⊆ U and spt V = U ∩ spt mu
O is open and mu(O) = 0 by second countability (Measure.measure_compl_support)
withDensity on the measurable set O: the integral of ofReal(theta) against H^n restricted to O ∩ M is 0, so theta ≤ 0 H^n-a.e. on O ∩ M
theta > 0 on M forces H^n(O ∩ M) = 0, hence H^n(M \ spt V) = 0

No density assumption or circular dependency is introduced. The bare declaration name is unreserved.

subproblem.title: Upper Density Theorem in the contract normalization (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6)
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, nu any measure on R^(n+l), and A ⊆ R^(n+l) a nu-null-measurable set with nu(A) < infinity. Here nu is defined on the Borel sigma-algebra and evaluated on arbitrary sets through its outer measure; no local finiteness is assumed. Then H^n({x : x ∉ A and limsup_{r -> 0+} nu(A ∩ B_r(x)) / ofReal(omega_n r^n) ≠ 0}) = 0. Here B_r(x) is the closed ball, omega_n = unitBallVolume n = pi^(n/2)/Gamma(n/2+1), the quotient is ENNReal division in [0, infinity], and H^n = muHE[n]. In words: the upper density Theta^{*n}(nu, A, x) vanishes for H^n-a.e. x outside A.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (A : Set (Amb n ℓ)), NullMeasurableSet A ν → ν A < ∞ → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) {x | x ∉ A ∧ limsup (fun r : ℝ => ν (A ∩ closedBall x r) / ENNReal.ofReal (unitBallVolume n * r ^ n)) (𝓝[>] 0) ≠ 0} = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.6 (Upper Density Theorem). This is the fact (Leb) used in step 3 of the parent proof. The pinned SimonGMT library formalizes it as Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6 (Chapter01/DensityComparison.lean:332). That version holds in an arbitrary metric space and for every real dimension >= 0, including n = 0, and needs no local finiteness of the measure. The module Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.DensityComparison is not imported, even transitively, by the contract. So the Lean file proving this child must add `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.DensityComparison`. Submission.lean is not byte-checked by the comparator, and only the definitions used by the frozen statement must stay unchanged. This child only transports the theorem to the contract normalization.

Notation:
- X = R^(n+l), a metric space with its Borel sigma-algebra.
- nu° is the outer measure of nu (nu.toOuterMeasure).
- w_n := ofReal(pi^(n/2)/Gamma(n/2+1)), which is SimonGMT's realUnitBallVolume n.
- For an outer measure m and a set A, Theta^{*n}(m, A, x) = limsup_{r -> 0+} m(A ∩ B_r(x)) / (w_n (ofReal r)^n). This is Simon's upper density (3.1), SimonGMT dimensionalUpperDensity.
- H^n_S is Simon's Hausdorff measure (SimonGMT simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n).
- muH[n] is the unnormalized Hausdorff measure.

1. nu° is Borel regular in Simon's sense. Every Borel set is nu-measurable, hence Caratheodory-measurable for nu°. Every set S has a measurable (Borel) hull B ⊇ S with nu(B) = nu(S) (exists_measurable_superset). This is SimonGMT measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular nu.
2. A is Caratheodory-measurable for nu°. Since A is nu-null-measurable, nu(T) = nu(T ∩ A) + nu(T \ A) for every T ⊆ X (measure_inter_add_sdiff₀). Moreover nu°(A) = nu(A) < infinity.
3. The quotients agree. First, omega_n >= 0, because pi^(n/2) > 0 and Gamma(n/2+1) > 0 (n/2+1 > 0, Real.Gamma_pos_of_pos). For r > 0 we then have ofReal(omega_n r^n) = ofReal(omega_n) ofReal(r^n) = w_n (ofReal r)^n (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_pow, ENNReal.rpow_natCast; ofReal(omega_n) is definitionally w_n). So for every x and every r > 0, the quotient nu(A ∩ B_r(x)) / ofReal(omega_n r^n) in the statement equals Simon's quotient nu°(A ∩ B_r(x)) / (w_n (ofReal r)^n). The two functions of r agree on (0, infinity), which belongs to the filter of right neighbourhoods of 0, so their limsups along that filter agree (limsup_congr). Thus the limsup in the statement is Theta^{*n}(nu°, A, x), and the set in the statement is E := {x : x ∉ A and Theta^{*n}(nu°, A, x) ≠ 0}.
4. H^n_S(E) = 0, by the Upper Density Theorem. Printed proof of Simon 3.6:
   - Let t > 0, let S_t = {x ∈ X \ A : Theta^{*n}(nu°, A, x) >= t}, and let C be any closed subset of A.
   - X \ C is open and S_t ⊆ X \ A ⊆ X \ C. Hence Theta^{*n}(nu°, A ∩ (X \ C), x) = Theta^{*n}(nu°, A, x) >= t for x ∈ S_t, since the density depends only on A near x.
   - Apply the Comparison Theorem 3.3 with nu° restricted to A, S_t and X \ C in place of mu, A_1 and A_2. Here S_t ⊆ X \ C, and 3.3 needs only that Borel sets are Caratheodory-measurable (mul_simonHausdorff_le_of_le_dimensionalUpperDensity). Borel sets remain Caratheodory-measurable for nu° restricted to A, by Simon's remark after 1.12 (SimonGMT isCaratheodoryMeasurable_restrict). This gives t H^n_S(S_t) <= nu°(A \ C) for each closed C ⊆ A.
   - By 1.15(2) (nu° Borel regular, A measurable, nu°(A) < infinity, X metric) there are closed C_j ⊆ A with nu°(A \ C_j) -> 0. So H^n_S(S_t) = 0.
   - Take t = 1/i, i = 1, 2, .... Every x ∈ E has Theta^{*n}(nu°, A, x) > 0, hence lies in some S_{1/i}. Countable subadditivity gives H^n_S(E) = 0.
   In Lean this whole step is simon_theorem_3_6 nu° (step 1) (0 <= n) (step 2) (nu°(A) < infinity).
5. Null sets transfer. As outer measures, H^n_S = (w_n / 2^n) muH[n] (SimonGMT simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal_eq_scaled_hausdorffMeasure, valid since n >= 0). The factor w_n / 2^n is nonzero, because w_n > 0 (realUnitBallVolume_pos) and 2^n < infinity (ENNReal.div_ne_zero). Hence step 4 gives muH[n](E) = 0. Finally muHE[n] = c muH[n] with c = addHaarScalarFactor(volume, muH[n]) (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, Measure.smul_apply). So muHE[n](E) = c · 0 = 0.
6. By step 3 the set in the statement is E, so its muHE[n]-measure is 0.
proof_key_steps: The outer measure nu° of nu is Borel regular, and A is Caratheodory-measurable for nu° (as A is null-measurable) with nu°(A) < infinity
For r > 0 the contract quotient nu(A ∩ B_r(x))/ofReal(omega_n r^n) equals Simon's quotient (3.1), so the limsups along r -> 0+ agree and the set is E = {x ∉ A : Theta^{*n}(nu°, A, x) ≠ 0}
Simon's Upper Density Theorem 3.6 (SimonGMT simon_theorem_3_6; printed proof via 3.3 and 1.15(2)) gives H^n_S(E) = 0
H^n_S and muHE[n] are nonzero finite multiples of muH[n], so muHE[n](E) = 0

audit.reason: The proposition exactly expresses the stated exceptional-set conclusion for a finite null-measurable A and arbitrary Borel measure. Every proof step is justified: Borel regularity of the induced outer measure, Caratheodory measurability of A, eventual equality of ENNReal quotients, Simon 3.6, and transfer through the nonzero Hausdorff normalization factor. No local finiteness or positive-dimension hypothesis is missing. The additional import is permitted, the proof is complete and independent, and the bare name is unreserved.

subproblem.title: Support minus carrier is H^n-null under positive density (Simon 4.10(1) with the Upper Density Theorem)
subproblem.statement: Let U be any subset of R^(n+l) and V = v(M, theta) a rectifiable n-varifold in U (contract structure) with weight mu. Suppose every x ∈ spt V = U ∩ spt mu has a positive density: there is a real t > 0 with mu(B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) -> t as r -> 0+ (V.HasDensity x t; closed balls, quotient in [0, infinity]). Then H^n(spt V \ M) = 0, where H^n = muHE[n].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {n ℓ : ℕ} {U : Set (Amb n ℓ)} (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U), (∀ x ∈ V.support, ∃ t : ℝ, 0 < t ∧ V.HasDensity x t) → (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (V.support \ V.carrier) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1(a) and 3 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 4, Remark 4.10(1)). The Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6) is supplied by sibling upper_density_null (Lean name upperDensity_ne_zero_outside_hausdorff_null).

Notation: H^n = muHE[n] on X = R^(n+l); M = V.carrier; mu = V.weight = (H^n restricted to M) with density ofReal(theta); spt V = U ∩ spt mu; B_r are closed balls and B'_r open balls. V.HasDensity x t means mu(B_r(x)) / ofReal(omega_n r^n) -> ofReal(t) in [0, infinity] as r -> 0+, with omega_n = unitBallVolume n. No openness of U and no lower bound on n is used.

1. Basic facts.
   (a) mu << H^n restricted to M (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous). Also (H^n restricted to M)(X \ M) = H^n((X \ M) ∩ M) = H^n(∅) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply₀', M H^n-null-measurable). Hence mu(X \ M) = 0, and consequently mu(S ∩ M) = mu(S) for every set S (measure_inter_conull).
   (b) M is mu-null-measurable. It is H^n-null-measurable; H^n restricted to M ≤ H^n, so H^n restricted to M << H^n; and mu << H^n restricted to M (NullMeasurableSet.mono_ac).
2. Finite-mass radii. Let N := spt V \ M and x ∈ N. As x ∈ spt V, the hypothesis gives t with mu(B_r(x))/ofReal(omega_n r^n) -> ofReal(t) as r -> 0+. Since ofReal(t) < infinity, the quotient is < infinity for all sufficiently small r > 0, because [0, infinity) is a neighbourhood of ofReal(t). Choose such an r_x > 0. Then mu(B_{r_x}(x)) < infinity: otherwise the quotient would be infinity / ofReal(omega_n r_x^n) = infinity, as the denominator is finite (ENNReal.top_div_of_ne_top).
3. Countable subcover. The open balls B'_{r_x}(x), x ∈ N, cover N, since x ∈ B'_{r_x}(x) as r_x > 0. R^(n+l) is second countable, so there is a countable T ⊆ N such that the union of B'_{r_y}(y) over y ∈ T equals the union of B'_{r_x}(x) over x ∈ N (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_biUnion_countable). Hence N ⊆ union over y ∈ T of (N ∩ B'_{r_y}(y)). By countable subadditivity (measure_biUnion_null_iff) it suffices to prove H^n(N ∩ B'_{r_y}(y)) = 0 for each y ∈ T.
4. Fix y ∈ T and put A := M ∩ B_{r_y}(y). A is mu-null-measurable, by 1(b) and because closed balls are Borel. Also mu(A) <= mu(B_{r_y}(y)) < infinity by step 2, since y ∈ N. By sibling upper_density_null applied to nu := mu and this A, the set E_y := {x : x ∉ A and limsup_{rho -> 0+} mu(A ∩ B_rho(x))/ofReal(omega_n rho^n) ≠ 0} has H^n(E_y) = 0.
5. N ∩ B'_{r_y}(y) ⊆ E_y. Let x ∈ N ∩ B'_{r_y}(y).
   (i) x ∉ M, hence x ∉ A.
   (ii) Since B'_{r_y}(y) is open, there is eps > 0 with B'_eps(x) ⊆ B'_{r_y}(y). For 0 < rho < eps we have B_rho(x) ⊆ B'_eps(x) ⊆ B'_{r_y}(y) ⊆ B_{r_y}(y). So A ∩ B_rho(x) = B_rho(x) ∩ M, and by 1(a), mu(A ∩ B_rho(x)) = mu(B_rho(x)). Thus the quotients mu(A ∩ B_rho(x))/ofReal(omega_n rho^n) and mu(B_rho(x))/ofReal(omega_n rho^n) agree for all rho ∈ (0, eps), a set in the filter of right neighbourhoods of 0.
   (iii) As x ∈ spt V, the hypothesis gives t > 0 with mu(B_rho(x))/ofReal(omega_n rho^n) -> ofReal(t). By (ii) the A-quotient has the same limit (Tendsto.congr'). Along the nontrivial filter of right neighbourhoods of 0, the limsup of a convergent function is its limit (Tendsto.limsup_eq). So the limsup equals ofReal(t), which is ≠ 0 because t > 0. Hence x ∈ E_y.
6. Therefore H^n(N ∩ B'_{r_y}(y)) <= H^n(E_y) = 0 for every y ∈ T, and by step 3, H^n(spt V \ M) = H^n(N) = 0.
proof_key_steps: mu vanishes off M (mu << H^n restricted to M) and M is mu-null-measurable
Positive finite density at each x ∈ N = spt V \ M gives r_x > 0 with mu(B_{r_x}(x)) < infinity
Second countability: countably many open balls B'_{r_y}(y), y ∈ T ⊆ N, cover N, reducing to each N ∩ B'_{r_y}(y)
Apply sibling upper_density_null to nu = mu and A = M ∩ B_{r_y}(y), which is null-measurable with finite mass
For x ∈ N ∩ B'_{r_y}(y): x ∉ A and mu(A ∩ B_rho(x)) = mu(B_rho(x)) for small rho, so the limsup equals ofReal(t) > 0 and x lies in the H^n-null exceptional set

audit.reason: The prose and exact proposition retain the positive finite density hypothesis on all of V.support. The proof establishes concentration on the carrier and its weight-null-measurability, obtains finite-mass radii from ENNReal convergence, takes a countable open-ball cover, and meets both hypotheses of upper_density_null. Local equality of ball masses then makes each relevant limsup strictly positive, placing the difference inside countably many null exceptional sets. The declared dependency is sufficient and correctly directed; no parent theorem is used. The bare name is unreserved.
